authored.observedEffect: Mechanical PURE_C and direct pinned compiler/assembler diagnostics emit 828 bytes/207 instructions with the same 88-byte frame. The compiler keeps owner in s8 before the first flag test and spills the owner cursor to the stack, reversing the retail owner/cursor lifetime arrangement. Both-cursor typing has the same regression. Other-cursor-only typing and a register qualifier on strongest_adjustment retain the baseline 824-byte instruction words and 25 aligned relocation-masked differences. Diagnostic alignment of the 828-byte trial is broadly shifted and is not a linked score.
authored.remainingFailure: The 828-byte source cannot replace the accepted 824-byte owner and is not selected. C3902FE42E remains best; the result does not eliminate typed-cursor or loop-lifetime hypotheses in other source contexts. No production, table-ownership or complete W5 verifier change occurred. GoldOx received the specific allocator question in mail 454; no tooling defect is supported.
